Ratan vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:2561) on 17 January,
2024
Author: Dinesh Mehta

Bench: Dinesh Mehta [2024:RJ-JD:2561] HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT JODHPUR S.B.
Criminal Miscellaneous Bail Application No. 438/2024 Ratan S/o Laxman Gurjar, Aged About 31 Years, R/o Shiv Nagar, Gurla, Karoi Police Station, District Bhilwara.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE FOR RAJASTHAN AT JODHPUR
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
(Lodged In District Jail Bhilwara.)
----Petitioner Versus 1. State Of Rajasthan, through Public Prosecutor 2. Maya Gurjar W/o Narain Gurjar, R/o Rampuriya, Karoi Police Station, Bhilwara, District Bhilwara.
----Respondents For Petitioner(s) : Mr. N.K. Gurjar
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Arun Kumar, Public Prosecutor  JUSTICE DINESH MEHTA  Order 17/01/2024 1.

This application for bail has been filed by the applicant under section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 in connection with FIR No.178/2023, registered at Police Station Karoi, District Bhilwara for the offence under section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the FIR has been lodged vindictively, when the relationship between the applicant and the prosecutrix turned sour.

3. Learned counsel further submitted that even if any physical relationship was established between the prosecutrix and the applicant, the same was with consent and thus, the applicant who [2024:RJ-JD:2561] (2 of 3) [CRLMB-438/2024] is behind the bars since 11.12.2023

is entitled to be Ratan vs State Of Rajasthan (2024:Rj-Jd:2561) on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153934433/
1 enlarged on bail.

4. Learned Public Prosecutor vehemently opposed the bail application by contending that in the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the prosecutrix has alleged forceful sexual assault under allurement of getting her husband released from Jail and under threat to her and her children's life.

5. Heard learned counsel for the applicant and the learned Public Prosecutor and perused the material available on record including the statements under sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
6.

A perusal of the FIR and the statements reveals that the first incident of sexual assault (if any)
took place at least two years ago of the date of filing of the FIR and still the prosecutrix continued to be in touch with and indulged in physical relationship with the present applicant.

The possibility that the FIR has been lodged vindictively or to save humiliation when the relationship between the prosecutrix and the applicant became sour or came to light, cannot be ruled out.
7. Upon perusal of the record, this Court also finds that the objectionable photographs which the prosecutrix has alleged to be made viral by the applicant, have been found from the mobile phone of none other than the prosecutrix herself.

8. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court deems it just and proper to grant bail to the accused- applicant under section 439 Cr.P.C.
[2024:RJ-JD:2561] (3 of 3) [CRLMB-438/2024]
9.
Consequently, the bail application filed under section 439 Cr.P.C. is allowed.

The applicant Ratan S/o Laxman Gurjar, arrested in connection with FIR No.178/2023, registered at Police Station Karoi, District Bhilwara, shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- and two sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
10. Applicant shall be required to appear before that Court on all dates of hearing and as and when called upon to do so.
11. Needless to mention that the above observations made by this Court are on the basis of material so far produced before the Court.

These are only prima-facie observations and the same shall however, not come in the way of the trial Court to take independent view of the matter, based on ocular and oral evidence, while finally deciding the case.

(DINESH MEHTA),J 112-Ramesh/-
